title: Clopen irreducible components of an etale scheme over a normal base
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth] whose local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $q:Z\to X$ be etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then $Z$ is locally topologically Noetherian (every point of $Z$ has an open neighbourhood whose underlying topological space is Noetherian, i.e. satisfies the descending chain condition on closed subsets) and geometrically unibranch (for every $z\in Z$, a strict henselization [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] of $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ has irreducible spectrum), and every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $|Z|$ is open and closed in $|Z|$. Consequently every connected component of $|Z|$ (a maximal nonempty connected subset [def-weil-connected-scheme]) is irreducible and is open and closed in $|Z|$. The scheme $Z$ may be empty.

source.place: proof of Lemma 7.4.10, p. 71, first paragraph; normal implies geometrically unibranch by Stacks properties.tex Tag 0BQ3

proof.text: By [def-weil-etale-morphism], $q$ is locally of finite presentation, so by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] every $z\in Z$ lies in an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $q(U)$ contained in an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$ and $A\cong R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ as $R$-algebras. Such an $A$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by the images of the $t_i$, so $R\to A$ is of finite type, and the pointwise criterion [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] shows that $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to the given locally Noetherian $X$: $Z$ is locally Noetherian. Choose affine Noetherian open neighbourhoods in $Z$ by [pqf-def-locnoeth]; each has Noetherian underlying space by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. Thus $Z$ is locally topologically Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01TW, label lemma-finite-presentation-finite-type, with Tag 01T2, label lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize; Tag 01T6, label lemma-finite-type-noetherian; properties.tex Tag 01OZ, label lemma-Noetherian-topology

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open with section ring $R$. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $R_{\mathfrak p}$ with a local ring of $X$. It is therefore a normal domain by hypothesis. Hence $R$ is a normal ring, exactly by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring].

The affine-local description in [def-weil-etale-morphism] covers $Z$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ mapping into affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$, with $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ etale. Step 2 makes $R$ normal, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal] makes $B$ normal. For $z\in W$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ with $B_{\mathfrak q_z}$, a normal domain by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Consequently all stalks of $Z$ are integrally closed domains.

source.place: Tag 033C, label lemma-normal-goes-up, etale specialization; schemes.tex Tag 01HV

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. It is a normal domain by step 3. Its prime localizations are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], so $A$ is also a normal ring in the terminology of [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Choose a separable closure $K$ of its residue field and a strict henselization $C$ as in [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Its pointed etale indexing category is essentially small and filtered by [lem-sc-pointed-etale-small-filtered], and $C$ is local by [lem-sc-ring-strict-henselization-local-maximal-ideal]. The defining colimit is therefore a filtered colimit of etale $A$-algebras with local vertex. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain](a): $C$ is a normal domain. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2), $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is integral, hence irreducible by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. This proves the precise strict-henselization formulation of geometric unibranchness in the item, for every $z$.

source.place: Tag 06DI, label lemma-henselization-normal; algebra.tex Tags 04GP and 04GW; properties.tex Tag 0BQ3, label lemma-normal-geometrically-unibranch

proof.text: Let $C$ be an irreducible component of $|Z|$ and let $z\in C$. Choose an affine Noetherian open neighbourhood $W$ of $z$ using step 1. Its stalks are the corresponding stalks of $Z$, hence normal by step 3. Apply clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal] to $W$: its irreducible components are pairwise disjoint and open and closed in $W$. By [lem-sc-components-open-injection], $C\cap W$ is one of these components, since it contains $z$. Thus $C\cap W$ is open in $W$, hence open in $Z$. Taking the union of these neighbourhoods as $z$ ranges over $C$ proves that $C$ is open. It is closed because irreducible components are closed [def-weil-irreducible-components].

source.place: Tag 0357, label lemma-normal-locally-finite-nr-irreducibles, affine-open argument; Tag 033M, label lemma-normal-Noetherian

proof.text: If two irreducible components $C,D$ of $Z$ meet at $z$, choose the same $W$ as in step 5. Their restrictions are components of $W$ by [lem-sc-components-open-injection]; disjointness of the components of $W$, supplied by clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal], forces $C\cap W=D\cap W$. Injectivity in [lem-sc-components-open-injection] then gives $C=D$. Thus the irreducible components of $Z$ are pairwise disjoint.

Let $T$ be a connected component of $|Z|$, in the nonempty convention of [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Choose $z\in T$ and an irreducible component $C$ containing $z$, using [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. By step 5, $C$ is clopen. The disjoint relatively clopen subsets $T\cap C$ and $T\setminus C$ partition $T$; the first is nonempty, so connectedness forces $T\subseteq C$. Every irreducible space is connected: a partition into two nonempty clopen sets would be a union of two proper closed subsets, contrary to [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Therefore $C$ is connected and maximality of the connected component $T$ gives $T=C$. Thus $T$ is irreducible and clopen. When $Z$ is empty there are neither irreducible components nor nonempty connected components, so all assertions remain valid.
